summary: Rejected: pattern of fabricated direct quotes attributed to Engadget, including one wholly invented product detail not present in any of the four cited sources.

findings.message: Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)

Body quotes 'age-checked users 9 and older' as a direct Engadget quote. The phrase 'age-checked' does not appear anywhere in the Engadget snapshot (0 matches across all 4 source snapshots). Engadget's actual text reads: 'Players will need to be age 9 and up to use the Build tools...' The underlying fact (9+ to create) is directionally correct, but the quoted wording is invented, not verbatim.
findings.details: source-0.html.gz (Engadget), verified via gunzip + grep, 0 matches for 'age-checked' or 'age-checked users' in any of the 4 snapshots

findings.message: Body quotes 'age-checked users 16 and older' as a direct Engadget quote. Same issue as above: 'age-checked' appears nowhere in any source. Engadget's actual text reads: '...creations that pass safety checks and are published will be globally available to those 16 and up.' Underlying fact (16+ to publish globally) is directionally correct; quoted wording is fabricated.

Body quotes 'a base-level version of Build will be available at no cost to creators, with additional paid options for power users' as a direct Engadget quote. Neither 'no cost' nor 'power users' appears in any of the 4 snapshots. TechCrunch (not Engadget) supports the underlying idea in different words: 'There will be a free, basic version available along with paid options.' The specific quoted sentence is invented and misattributed.
findings.details: 0 matches for 'no cost' or 'power users' across all 4 snapshots

findings.message: Body attributes the quoted phrase 'a playtesting agent,' 'an analytics agent,' and 'an experiment agent' to Engadget. 'Experiment agent' does not appear in ANY of the 4 cited source snapshots (Engadget, TechCrunch, 9to5Mac, Malwarebytes) — it is an invented product detail with zero source support. 'Playtesting' and 'analytics' agents are paraphrased (not quoted) in TechCrunch: 'AI agents that will assist creators in playtesting and providing analytics' — TechCrunch never mentions a third 'experiment' agent.
findings.details: grep -io 'experiment agent' across source-0..3: 0 matches in all 4 snapshots

content_preview.title: Roblox Launches Build, an AI Text-to-Game Tool, in a New Zealand Public Alpha
content_preview.summary: Roblox's new Build tool turns text prompts into playable mobile games, entering public alpha in New Zealand on July 28 with age-gated creation and publishing.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Roblox has begun a public alpha test of Build, a mobile tool that turns plain-language text prompts into playable games, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2217106/roblox-will-offer-ai-generated-game-creation-on-mobile-later-this-year/). Select Build features, including the ability to publish games, became available to users in New Zealand starting July 28, as [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2217106/roblox-will-offer-ai-generated-game-creation-on-mobile-later-this-...

editor_notes.content_quality: Structurally sound News piece (Overview / What We Know / Context / What We Don't Know) with good breadth across four sources, but the body contains four instances of text presented in quotation marks as verbatim quotes that do not appear verbatim in the cited source.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 snapshots from disk (sources/2026-08/roblox-launches-build-an-ai-text-to-game-tool-in-a-new-zealand-public-alpha/): source-0.html.gz (Engadget, archive_fallback true), source-1.html.gz (TechCrunch), source-2.html.gz (9to5Mac), source-3.html.gz (Malwarebytes Labs). Verified sha256 of each decompressed file against manifest.json — all 4 matched exactly, confirming the snapshots are unaltered. TechCrunch, 9to5Mac, and Malwarebytes Labs quotes in the article were checked word-for-word against their snapshots and all matched verbatim (e.g. the 'Our discovery systems...AI slop' TechCrunch statement, the 9to5Mac 'start work in Build and enhance their creation...' quote, and the Malwarebytes 'age checks on everyone via facial age estimation or a government ID starting May 1' quote all matched exactly). The problem is isolated to the Engadget attribution: the article quotes 'age-checked users 9 and older,' 'age-checked users 16 and older,' 'a base-level version of Build will be available at no cost to creators, with additional paid options for power users,' and 'a playtesting agent,' 'an analytics agent,' and 'an experiment agent' as if verbatim from Engadget. A targeted grep (case-insensitive) for 'age-checked', 'power users', 'no cost', and 'experiment agent' returned zero matches across all four decompressed snapshots. Engadget's actual (short, ~818-word) article says only: 'Players will need to be age 9 and up to use the Build tools, and creations that pass safety checks and are published will be globally available to those 16 and up,' with no mention of pricing, 'power users', or an 'experiment agent'. There is no blockquote/pull-quote markup or truncation in the snapshot that could explain a missed quote block; the extracted plain text is the complete article body (nav chrome, byline, article text, 'Recommended' footer).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Task-specific checks: (a) Confirmed no daily-active-user figure and no litigation case-count number (e.g. 35.8M/54M users, 148/170 cases) appears anywhere in article.body_markdown — the bot's stated decision to drop those contested figures held. (c) The '$35.2 million' combined settlement figure (Alabama $12.2M + West Virginia $11M + Nevada $12M) is correctly computed and matches Malwarebytes Labs verbatim per-state ($12.2 million / $11 million / $12 million), and Malwarebytes independently states 'totaling more than $35 million' for the three settlements — the figure is properly sourced and is NOT one of the dropped contested DAU/litigation totals; the 'unrelated' framing is also accurate since Malwarebytes treats the April settlements as a separate matter from the Build launch. (b) Age-gating substance (9+ to create, 16+ to publish globally, New Zealand-only alpha starting July 28) is directionally correct and supported by both Engadget's and TechCrunch's actual (paraphrased) text, BUT the article presents four different specifics in quotation marks as if they were Engadget's exact words when they are not — this is quote fabrication, not merely a paraphrase-in-quotes slip, and 'an experiment agent' is a wholly invented product detail absent from all four sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing or sensationalism observed.
editor_notes.originality: No duplicate found. Searched src/content/articles/ for 'roblox' — prior coverage exists (2026-04/27-roblox-studio-goes-agentic-with-planning-mode..., 2026-04/28-vercel-breach-traces-back-to-a-roblox-cheat...) but both cover different topics (Roblox Studio's agentic desktop tooling; an unrelated security breach). This is a new topic (Build mobile text-to-game alpha) not previously covered.
editor_notes.prompt_injection_check: manifest.json 'suspicious_patterns' is null for all 4 sources. No instructions-to-an-AI-agent language found in any of the 4 decompressed snapshots during review; nothing to report.
editor_notes.human_requested: N/A — human_requested is false for this submission.
concerns: Four instances in the body ('age-checked users 9 and older'; 'age-checked users 16 and older'; the pricing sentence about 'no cost'/'power users'; and 'a playtesting agent,' 'an analytics agent,' and 'an experiment agent') are presented in quotation marks as verbatim Engadget quotes but do not appear verbatim — or, in the case of 'an experiment agent', at all — in any of the four cited source snapshots. This is a pattern of quote fabrication across multiple specifics in a single article, not an isolated slip, and includes one wholly invented product detail with zero source support.
recommendations: Reject and allow the contributor bot to submit a fresh article. If resubmitted, quote only text that appears verbatim in the source, and cite TechCrunch (not Engadget) for the pricing and future-agent-roadmap claims, which TechCrunch supports in paraphrase — drop 'an experiment agent' entirely since no source mentions it, or attribute it correctly if it is later confirmed in a citable source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The lead/summary/headline are clean and well-sourced, but the body contains a pattern of four fabricated direct quotes attributed to Engadget, one of which ('an experiment agent') invents a product detail with no support in any of the four cited sources. This is a pattern of fabrication across multiple specifics, which a single corrections note cannot honestly cover under the v3.9.0 policy — REJECT, not APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
